about: The LARRYD runtime's own config. It is air gapped: its ONLY link to the platform is HTTP to the addresses below, signed with the secret named here. No path, file, database or module of the platform is ever named.

platform.about: where the runtime calls the platform, per side (the platform's global_config offices: rnd = the stage, pf = live)

callers.about: the offices that may call the runtime's /api (X-Office), each checked with the secret

secret.name: runtime_link
secret.purpose: signs every call between the platform and the runtime; each side keeps its own copy in its own instance

intake.about: an agent the owner approved from LARRYD's review queue (one .larryd file) becomes a locker folder <folder>/<card key>/ (the host's place command)

makes.about: THE OUTSIDE HAND (core_engine/outside.py): what an agent may ask LARRYD to have made by a model on its list (Nano Banana 2, Seedance 2.5). a_day: how many files of each kind ONE member may have made by ONE agent in a day (UTC); the provider is paid per file with the platform's own key (its one home is FROST's vault; the runtime asks for it per errand and keeps no copy), so this is the bill's guard. The owner's numbers.

slots.about: Cloud Run (the LARRYD runtime design): the one runtime serves every caller; a call's key id names who called (slot-a, slot-b, proof), and the runtime calls back THAT caller at <host>/<office>, signed with its own key 'runtime-to-<caller>'. A caller with no host here is never called back (slot A has none until it runs the new platform; the laptop's proof has none: it cannot be reached).

access.about: THE SECOND GUARD (the owner: two guards, never one): every hire and run the platform signs carries the platform's own access decision for the member (FROST's grid) in this field; the runtime refuses any hire or run whose signed body does not carry the value that grants. The field's name is the hire-rights lane's (provisional until it is named).

pages.about: THE PAGES' OWN ADDRESS of each caller (the owner, 2026-10-25, THE LARRY DATA FABRIC's DOWNLOAD): where its members open their pages, so a link the runtime builds for a page (DA-M's own download of a file) is an https address of that very host, in a new tab (the platform's view gate takes nothing else). A caller with none here gets no such link.
